meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid - Civil law (Spanish/Gran-Colombian tradition) overlaid with common-law-inspired statutory commercial, foundation, maritime and banking law; unitary national legal system with no sub-state tax distinctions
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: United States-Panama Trade Promotion Agreement (TPA; in force since 31 October 2012)
United States-Panama Bilateral Investment Treaty (BIT; in force since 11 May 1991)
Panama-Singapore Free Trade Agreement (in force since 12 July 2006)
Panama-Peru Free Trade Agreement (in force since 1 May 2012)

Panama double taxation treaty network under a territorial tax model (DTAAs in force with, inter alia, Mexico, Korea, France, Spain, Portugal, Netherlands, Luxembourg, Singapore, United Arab Emirates, Qatar and Barbados)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law 23 of 27 April 2015 on AML/CFT (as amended by Law 70 of 31 December 2019); Executive Decree 363 of 7 December 2015 (implementing regulation); Law 129 of 18 March 2020 creating the Registro de Transparencia y Beneficiario Final (RTBF); Executive Decree 194 of 16 November 2021 (RTBF regulation); Law 25 of 12 June 1995 on Private Interest Foundations (as amended by Law 61 of 2015 and Law 15 of 6 July 2018)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public of the country of origin (authenticating corporate minutes)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copies of passports/identity documents of the founder, Foundation Council members and protector (if any)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public of the country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization for non-Hague jurisdictions)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based customer due diligence under Law 23/2015 and Decree 363/2015: verify founder, Foundation Council, protector and ultimate beneficiaries; screen against the OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council consolidated list, EU consolidated sanctions list and Panama's UAF national terrorism list; Enhanced Due Diligence is mandatory for foreign and domestic PEPs (Law 70/2019), persons in FATF-listed high-risk jurisdictions, and anomalous source-of-funds transactions; continuous transaction monitoring and annual refresh of the UBO file in the RTBF.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Público de Panamá - Servicios en Línea (Sede Electrónica; https://www.registro-publico.gob.pa) - name clearance module: Certificado de Diferencia de Nombre
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names must be submitted in Spanish/Latin script; the foundation name must contain or end with 'Fundación' or 'Foundation'; foreign-language names are accepted only transliterated into Latin characters; the proposed name must not be identical or visually/phonetically confusing with any existing registered entity; purely numeric designations are expressly permitted (e.g., 'Fundación 2025-0017').
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Banco / Banca / Bancario (prior approval of the Superintendency of Banks required)
Financiera / Finanzas / Crédito (banking-connotation; Superintendency of Banks approval)
Seguros / Aseguradora / Reaseguradora (insurance supervisory approval required)
Fiduciaria / Fideicomiso / Trust (fiduciary-business connotation; SBP license or waiver)
Fondo de Inversión / Valores / Bolsa (Securities Superintendency - SMV approval required)
Gobierno / República / Ministerio / Nacional / Oficial (state affiliation; prior ministerial authorization)
Militar / Policía / Defensa / Seguridad (official-security connotation; restricted)
Lotería / Casino / Juegos / Apuestas (gaming control authority approval required)
Caja de Ahorros / Cooperativa / Mutual (deposit-taking connotation; SBP approval)
Cruz Roja / UNICEF / Banco Mundial / Naciones Unidas (internationally protected institutional names; prohibited absent institutional consent)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The name-difference certificate is valid for 30 calendar days; no statutory extension exists, and a fresh certificate must be obtained if incorporation is not completed within the window. Upon rejection: (1) identify the conflicting registered name(s) via the online registry search; (2) re-file the certificate module with up to three alternative names in descending preference; (3) contest an adverse determination by filing a written 'Recurso de Reconsideración' with the Legal Department of the Registro Público within ten business days of the rejection notice; (4) pursue an administrative 'Recurso de Apelación' before the registry's senior administrative authority; and (5) exhaust judicial review before the Tercera Sala de lo Contencioso-Administrativo of the Corte Suprema de Justicia within the applicable statutory window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Acceptable for the foundation's operational address: an ISIC 6201 MarTech analytics SaaS holding may conduct business fully remotely and maintain no physical premises in Panama. The statutory registered office must nonetheless coincide with the physical office of the licensed Resident Agent in Panama City, where the foundation book, statutory records and the RTBF/UBO file must remain available for official inspection.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated below 5% annual probability of an unannounced physical inspection of the foundation's own premises (non-licensed, low-risk SaaS holding structure); however, the probability of UAF or supervisory inspection of the Resident Agent's physical office - where the foundation's statutory records are kept - is estimated at 25-40% annually, concentrated at the agent level rather than at the foundation.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law No. 25 of 12 June 1995 (Private Interest Foundations), as amended by Law No. 13 of 2008 and Law No. 52 of 2013; specifically Articles 2, 5, 18, 25 and 32 on formation, endowment, Foundation Council and registered agent.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado (Public Registry of Panama, Private Interest Foundations Section).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura Constitutiva de Fundación de Interés Privado (Foundation Charter), executed before a Panamanian Notary Public and inscribed in the Public Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is imposed by Panamanian law; the Foundation must declare an initial endowment of at least one asset or economic right, commonly US$100 or a single participating share. No escrow account is required for this private interest foundation vehicle.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The initial Board (Foundation Council), being duly constituted pursuant to Law 25, adopts the following resolutions. First, Endowment Subscription: the Foundation accepts the irrevocable endowment declared in the Foundation Charter and confirms that the minimum endowment requirement is satisfied. Second, Registered Office: the registered office of the Foundation is fixed at [Registered Address], Panama City, for the receipt of all legal and administrative notices. Third, Officers: the Council appoints [Name] as Chairperson, [Name] as Secretary, and [Name] as Treasurer, with full authority to open bank accounts, execute software service agreements, engage the registered agent, and represent the Foundation before the Public Registry and tax authorities. This Resolution is binding and effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Instruction and notarization of the Foundation Charter
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Panamanian Notary Public / licensed Panamanian attorney
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a licensed Panama attorney to draft the Spanish-language Escritura Constitutiva. The instrument must state the Foundation name, purpose, initial endowment, initial Foundation Council, beneficiaries and registered agent. The founder executes the instrument before a Panamanian notary, who incorporates it into the notarial protocol. Foreign identity documents must be notarized, apostilled or legalized as applicable.
required_dossiers: Foundation Charter draft in Spanish
Notarized copy of founder's passport or corporate identification
Proof or description of the initial endowment
Registered agent acceptance letter
Apostilled or legalized documents for non-Panamanian founders
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary identifies a formal deficiency in the draft, the attorney corrects the text and the instrument is re-executed before the same notary without restarting the entire incorporation process.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic filing and inscription at the Public Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Sección de Fundaciones de Interés Privado (Repuve online filing portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After notarization, submit the protocolized Foundation Charter for inscription. Use the Public Registry's Repuve electronic system or file directly at the Foundation Section. Pay the official state filing fee through Banco Nacional de Panamá or the authorized online treasury gateway and attach the payment voucher.
required_dossiers: Protocolized Escritura Constitutiva de Fundación
Application or cover letter signed by the registered agent
Official government fee payment receipt
Registered agent acceptance form
Consent of the initial Foundation Council members
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar issues an observación (formal query), the registered agent files a notarial corrective addendum addressing the stated defect. Where no objection is raised within the statutory period, the applicant may invoke the Public Registry's administrative silence remedy.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtaining the registration certificate and certified copies
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Público de Panamá — Certification Desk
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Once the inscription is completed, request certified copies of the registered Foundation Charter and the registry certificate confirming no pending observations. Verify the assigned foundation folio, date, and microfilm number. This certificate is the primary proof of legal existence for banks, payment service providers, and contractors.
required_dossiers: Registry filing receipt or control number
Identity document of the authorized requesting officer
Payment voucher for certified copy issuance
Power of attorney if a third party requests the copies
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains a typographical or data discrepancy, file a written rectification application with the Registry; urgent certified copies may be obtained using the registry's expedited certification service.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appointment of the licensed registered agent and adoption of registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Panamanian registered agent (law firm or corporate services provider)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute a registered agent agreement authorizing a Panama-licensed entity to act as the Foundation's statutory representative for receipt of legal and regulatory notices. The registered office address in Panama City is adopted by formal resolution. The agent's acceptance is filed with the Public Registry and recorded against the Foundation's file.
required_dossiers: Registered agent service agreement
Certified copy of the inscribed Foundation Charter
Board resolution adopting the registered office
Passport copies of the Foundation Council members
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the initially selected registered agent declines or becomes suspended, a substitute licensed agent is appointed and a change-of-agent notice is filed with the Public Registry; the Foundation's legal personality remains continuous.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Convening of the first Board (Foundation Council) meeting and execution of governance minutes
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the initial Foundation Council in accordance with the Charter, adopt the Pro-Forma First Board Resolution, and execute minutes confirming the endowment, registered office, and officer appointments. The signed minutes establish the signatory authority matrix for bank and SaaS payment provider onboarding.
required_dossiers: Meeting agenda
Initial endowment verification
Council member acceptance letters
Foundation Charter and identification documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a Council member is unavailable to attend in person, the meeting may be held by teleconference or videoconference where the Charter so permits; all minutes must be properly sealed by the Secretary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax registration and municipal operating pre-registration for commercial activity
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) and Municipality of Panama
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After the Public Registry inscription, if the Foundation intends to receive active service revenue from the SEO analytics tool, obtain the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) from DGI and file the Aviso de Operación or municipal patent with the Municipality of Panama. The activity is classified as a software/SaaS service, not an industrial manufacturing operation.
required_dossiers: Registry certificate of foundation inscription
Registered agent resolution
Founder and officer identification documents
Lease or ownership proof of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If DGI suspends the RUC application because of ambiguous business classification, submit a formal classification request referencing ISIC 6201 / NAICS 541511 and file an administrative reconsideration with the supporting Charter and service description.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — ISIC 6201 / NAICS 541511 corresponds to a non-physical software development and data analytics service; no industrial licensing authority exercises direct competence over this activity.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable. No industrial operating or manufacturing permit is required. A municipal Aviso de Operación may be obtained only if the Foundation elects to conduct active commercial billing operations in Panama.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente (MiAMBIENTE), Republic of Panama
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — the activity is an office-based SaaS and data analytics service with no physical infrastructure, no construction, and no extractive or industrial processes; therefore no environmental impact assessment, category registration, or environmental operating permit is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable — the activity generates no industrial wastewater, VOC emissions, process discharges, or hazardous waste. Office waste and recyclable e-waste must be handled through licensed municipal or private collection services; any future dedicated server-hosted infrastructure must comply with Panama's electronic waste and disposal regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The registered office must obtain a current fire safety compliance certificate from the Benemérito Cuerpo de Bomberos de Panamá (Panama Fire Department). Structural load and occupancy safety are evidenced by the municipal Certificate of Use and Occupancy issued by the Municipality of Panama; if employees are engaged, the Foundation must also satisfy the occupational health and hygiene obligations under Panamanian labor and social security law.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección General de Ingresos (DGI) of the Ministerio de Economía y Finanzas (MEF) — Panama's General Directorate of Revenue; official portal: SERTRACEN (https://sertracen.dgi.gob.pa) and the DGI e-Invoicing/SAE platform (https://www.dgi.gob.pa).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Panama Private Interest Foundation (PIF) without Panamanian-source activity is not obliged to hold a RUC; to commercialize the SEO analytics SaaS, the foundation first registers its charter in the Registro Público, appoints the resident agent/fiscal attorney, then files the RUC (Registro Único de Contribuyente) application with the DGI via SERTRACEN, attaching the foundation deed, public inscription certificate, identification of Foundation Council members, fiscal address confirmation, and a sworn economic-activity declaration; the ITBMS taxpayer registration is issued together with the RUC within 3-10 business days.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; Territorial_Scope — the PIF is taxed as a separate juridical person solely on Panamanian-source income under the territorial system; foreign-source revenue of the foundation stays outside Panama's income tax; no pass-through treatment is recognized for PIFs; tax-exempt zone treatment applies only if the PIF establishes operations in a registered free zone (e.g., SEM Panama Pacifico) and obtains zone authorization.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or equivalent classification election is available in Panamanian law; a PIF may, however, structure its actual business conduct to remain a non-commercial Law 25 foundation (no Panamanian-source profits and therefore no income tax or ITBMS obligation), or elect admitted ITBMS taxable-person status to operate a zero-rated digital export business; hybrid-mismatch and transparent-entity elections are not statutorily recognized.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: ITBMS — Impuesto de Transferencia de Bienes Muebles y Servicios (Panamanian value-added tax on transfers of movable goods and services)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: B/. (balboa at parity with USD): no minimum turnover threshold; registration is mandatory as soon as the PIF habitually carries out taxable transfers or renders services in Panamanian territory; the simplified small-taxpayer regime is available for annual gross income up to B/. 200,000; non-resident digital service providers are registrable without local turnover under the remote digital services rules.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing and centralized fiscal clearance through the DGI's SAE platform: each ITBMS invoice must be transmitted as a digitally signed XML document in real time to the DGI before delivery, must pass automated validation, and must contain the DGI-issued Sello Fiscal/QR clearance code; export invoices are additionally linked to the SIEC customs single-window; failures to clear invoices in advance trigger administrative fines, blocked input-credit claims, and presumption of non-issuance.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods physically exported from Panamanian customs territory and services rendered to non-resident customers — with performance, use, or enjoyment occurring abroad — qualify for the 0% ITBMS rate; the MarTech SEO content analytics SaaS qualifies when the subscriber is a foreign entity, the payment originates from outside Panama, and the analytics data is consumed abroad; the PIF must retain the executed SaaS agreement, non-resident customer documentation, and bank credit evidence; customary DGI practice expects the export consideration to be credited within 180 days of invoice date (not a positive-law deadline in Panama).
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Panama Electronic Customs Export Declaration (SIEC) — or a sworn Service Export Statement where digital delivery involves no physical goods movement
Commercial invoice and completed SaaS subscription/analytics agreement with the non-resident customer
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill, where physical goods or media are exported
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank credit advice from the overseas collection account evidencing receipt of the export proceeds
Beneficial ownership and end-customer register of the PIF demonstrating absence of Panamanian-domiciled users
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The DGI's export-audit unit verifies SIEC declarations, foundation banking records, and the foreign-destination nexus; if zero-rating is reversed, the full 10% ITBMS becomes payable with statutory interest computed from the invoice date; under Law 76 of 2019 tax-procedure rules, penalties range from 50% to 300% of the tax evaded plus administrative fines up to B/. 50,000; knowingly false export declarations expose the Foundation Council to criminal tax-fraud prosecution and clawback of input ITBMS credits.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco Nacional de Panamá (National Bank of Panama) serves as the government's fiscal agent; the Superintendencia de Bancos de Panamá (SBP) is the primary banking and foreign exchange regulator. Panama does not operate a traditional central bank.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Panama operates under a fully dollarised monetary system. The US dollar is legal tender and freely circulated alongside the on-demand fixed-balboa coinage. There are no exchange controls, and both current and capital account convertibility are unrestricted. Profit remittances, dividend distributions, and capital repatriation can be effected without FX approval or mandatory conversion. The sole practical hurdles are Panamanian withholding tax obligations on certain payments, documentary substantiation of underlying transactions, and AML/KYC verification standards imposed by the SBP-regulated banking system.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: There are no statutory export-proceeds surrender requirements or mandatory conversion ratios in Panama. Exporters may retain foreign exchange earnings in any currency, with no prescribed timeline for conversion or repatriation. The absence of a surrender burden is supported by the free use of the US dollar. Reporting duties under AML/CFT rules, such as declaration of cash and electronic transfers above thresholds, remain applicable to exporters and their financial institutions.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating for offshore digital EMI providers (e.g., Mercury, Airwallex, Payoneer) is Low for the PA_PIF because Panamanian law treats money transmission and payment services as banking activities requiring an SBP licence and local presence. Unlicensed offshore EMIs typically reject private interest foundations due to heightened overseas KYC friction and correspondent-bank constraints. Domestically licensed fintech payment providers operating under the SBP framework may achieve a Medium rating and can support cross-border clearing via BaaS arrangements with tier-1 banks, but they do not replace a physical banking relationship for foundation treasury management.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Directors and authorised signatories of the Private Interest Foundation are generally required to appear physically before the bank's compliance and account-opening team or before a Panamanian public notary during the final onboarding stage. Remote onboarding is possible only on a case-by-case basis, typically via notarised and apostilled corporate documents, verified passports, and a recorded video interview. For non-resident PIFs with nominee council members, most tier-1 banks insist on at least one physical meeting with the economic beneficial owner or a formally mandated legal representative in Panama.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque ownership arising from nominee foundation members and bearer shares
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete foundation charter with registration deed, updated council member register, notarised and apostilled identification of all beneficial owners, explicit written waiver of bearer instrument privileges, and a signed statement confirming the source and purpose of funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ambiguous source of wealth or high-risk jurisdiction exposure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Bank statements covering a substantive lookback period (12–36 months), audited financial statements of the foundation, tax returns, commercial contracts evidencing legitimate MarTech/SaaS revenue streams, and a narrative of wealth origination supported by external counsel or an independent wealth-management advisor.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between declared business model and expected transaction flows
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed business plan describing the SEO content analytics platform, subscription/client contracts, third-party payment processor statements (Stripe/Paddle), a projected transaction profile with expected counterparties and settlement percentages, and supporting licensing/exemption confirmations typical for low-risk software activities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions, PEP status, or adverse media screening flags
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Clear, tracible corporate genealogy and ultimate beneficial ownership map, OFAC/EU/UN sanctions screening report from a licensed provider, comprehensive adverse-media search results, and, where applicable, a qualified compliance opinion or clarifying legal memorandum addressing any PEP association.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound capital injections must be routed via SWIFT MT103 to the PIF's USD-denominated account at a Panamanian tier-1 bank. The wire must clearly specify the correct purpose code (e.g., 'Capital contribution' or 'Transfers under Article 13 of Foundation Charter') and identify the foundation's registered name and account number. To prevent rejection, the originator should provide a notarised board resolution recording the capital contribution, the foundation's charter excerpt, and a source-of-funds questionnaire. The Panamanian bank will verify the wiring instructions and, where the transfer exceeds regulatory thresholds, file an electronic money-laundering report. Use of a fully KYC-vetted correspondent bank in the US for USD clearing is mandatory.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for trade settlements are executed through SWIFT MT103 payment orders for direct supplier and vendor payments, documentary commercial letters of credit (MT700/MT710) for high-value or contractual imports/exports, and cross-border ACH rails for low-value SaaS subscription payments. For every disbursement, the foundation's authorised signatories must furnish an authenticated instruction, and the bank may require underlying invoices, commercial agreements, or tax-cleared status certificates. To support the platform's recurring software revenue, Paddle or Stripe payouts are cleared via daily aggregated ACH direct deposits into the foundation's operational account, then converted, when needed, to USD without FX controls.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable currency forwards on USD, EUR, and GBP crosses with licensed Panamanian and international banks
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for emerging-market currency exposures that are not freely deliverable in Panama
Cross-currency swaps to convert non-USD revenue streams into USD and manage long-term interest-rate exposures
FX options (European-style) used solely to hedge operational and balance-sheet currency risk

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foundation Government Fee (Tasa Anual Única de la Fundación de Interés Privado)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Panama Public Registry (Registro Público de Panamá) – Directorate General of Private Interest Foundations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually between January 1 and March 31; pre-payment covering the current calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% surcharge for payment made April 1 through June 30; 20% surcharge for payment made after July 1; administrative strike-off and dissolution proceedings initiated after 3 consecutive years of non-payment

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership (UBO) Registry Confirmation and Maintenance Filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Panama Public Registry (Registro Público de Panamá) – Beneficial Ownership Registry Unit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation aligned with the March 31 registration renewal cycle; any change in beneficial interest must be reported to the resident agent and filed within 30 days of the triggering event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines from US$5,000 to US$50,000 for non-filing, incomplete data, or false statements under Law 254 of 2019; the resident agent is jointly liable for late submission and registry corrections

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Income Tax Return (Declaración Jurada de Renta) or Non-Taxable Status Certificate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Panama Directorate General of Revenue (Dirección General de Ingresos – DGI, Ministry of Economy and Finance)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 3 months after the foundation's fiscal year-end (March 31 for calendar-year foundations); a nil or informative return is recommended where the foundation derives exclusively foreign-source income
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Monthly penalty interest at the statutory legal rate plus a 10% surcharge on any omitted tax; administrative fines for late filing; suspension of RUC tax registration and electronic filing privileges until compliance is restored

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Economic Substance Return (Declaración de Sustancia Económica) under Law 254 of 2019 and Executive Decree 242 of 2020
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually, concurrently with the income tax return window, within 3 months of fiscal year-end; mandatory only when the foundation engages in listed relevant activities in Panama, including holding or asset-management functions generating Panamanian-source income
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines up to US$200,000 for failure to file, inadequate substance, or false declarations; repeated violations may trigger registry strike-off and criminal referral for tax evasion under Panama's Tax Code

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Common Reporting Standard (CRS) Annual Declaration and Non-Financial Entity Self-Certification
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Panama Directorate General of Revenue (DGI) – Automatic Exchange of Information Unit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually in accordance with the DGI-published CRS calendar, typically between February and June for the preceding calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines under Panama's AEOI/CRS implementing rules; repeated non-compliance triggers heightened AML due diligence by Panamanian licensed banks and may impair the foundation's ability to obtain certificates of good standing

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No compulsory independent audit applies to Private Interest Foundations under Law 25 of 1995; an audit becomes mandatory only when the Foundation Charter expressly requires it, when the foundation conducts public securities offerings in Panama, or when a court-appointed supervisor orders an audit for beneficiary or creditor protection
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for SMEs or Panamanian Local GAAP accepted for general-purpose reporting; the foundation council must maintain accounting records adequate to determine territorial taxable income; full IFRS is recommended where the foundation consolidates into a multinational group or serves as a holding vehicle for cross-border SaaS and IP assets

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under Law 254 of 2019, the resident agent must file and continuously update the confidential beneficial ownership record with the Registro Público. A data confirmation and validation exercise is required annually at the same time as the March 31 fee renewal; any transfer, pledge, or substitution of beneficial participation in the foundation's assets or beneficiary rights must be reported within 30 days. Non-compliance exposes the foundation and the resident agent to fines of US$5,000 to US$50,000, plus potential Registry strike-off for aggravated default.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Beneficiaries and Founder Appointments
Minute Book (Libro de Actas) containing founder resolutions and foundation council meeting minutes

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$750 – US$1,500 per year (resident agent legal representation, registered office, registry coordination, and annual fee processing)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not statutorily required; voluntary certified audit engagement US$1,800 – US$4,500 per year depending on transaction volume and asset complexity

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% flat rate on net taxable income
